name: Buspirone
summary: Buspirone is a non-benzodiazepine anxiolytic with serotonergic activity. This profile remains research-only while generalized-anxiety efficacy, duration-of-evidence, serotonin-syndrome, CYP3A4 interaction, and regulatory evidence is assembled and reviewed.
description: Canonical buspirone entity for evidence and safety integration. Publication remains held until indication-specific scientific evidence, short- versus long-term treatment boundaries, serotonergic and metabolic interaction context, and regulatory provenance has passed the site’s review gates.
safety_notes: Current U.S. prescribing information contraindicates use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors intended to treat depression because of serotonin-syndrome and elevated-blood-pressure risk, warns about serotonin syndrome with serotonergic combinations, and notes clinically important CYP3A4 inhibitor/inducer interactions. Controlled long-term effectiveness beyond 3 to 4 weeks has not been demonstrated in the cited label. This summary is not exhaustive; consult current product-specific prescribing information.
